g_rules.text: Storytelling and connecting with the audience come first; tactics only amplify a story
First line is the hook and decides whether anyone reads on
Use hook formula families: curiosity, story, value ('How to X:'), contrarian ('Unpopular opinion:'), social proof
Fill the hook formula with a specific fact, number, or story
Ban contrast reveals ('It's not X, it's Y', 'Not because X. Because Y.', 'This isn't X. This is Y.')
Ban negation lists ('No X, no Y, no Z'); one plain absence is fine
Ban trailing pile-ons; end the sentence at the claim
Ban self-answered questions and colon reveals ('The result? ...', 'The best part: ...')
Ban stock/marketing phrases ('Say goodbye to', 'X, reimagined', 'Unlock the power of', 'next level', 'game-changer', 'Here's the thing')
No em dashes in posts; use a period or line break
No broetry; write paragraphs, break lines where a person would pause
No engagement bait ('Agree?', 'Thoughts?', 'Let that sink in'); end on the point or a real question
No manufactured vulnerability without a real story
No emoji as bullets or structure
Max one fragment / staccato burst per post
Max one list of three per post
No links in the post body; put links in the comments
LinkedIn content that works: personal stories with business lessons, contrarian takes, behind-the-scenes, data and original insights
Avoid overly promotional content
No generic motivational quotes
No corporate speak without personality
Front-load the hook before the 'see more' cut (~210 chars)
Use line breaks for readability
Target 1,200-1,500 characters
Max 3,000 characters
Tag people sparingly and genuinely
Use 3-5 hashtags
Hashtags at the end, not inline
Story Post template: hook, scene, challenge, what you tried, turning point, result, lesson, question
Contrarian Take template: unpopular opinion, what changed your mind with a number, reasons 1-3, recommendation, invite discussion
List Post template: 'X things I learned about [topic] after [credibility]:', numbered 'Point: explanation', wrap-up, 'Which resonates most?'
How-To template: 'How to [outcome] in [timeframe]:', steps with why/detail, result, CTA or question
End with a question to prompt engagement (comments weigh most)
Avoid uniform rhythm; vary sentence and paragraph length
Use 'is'/'has' instead of 'serves as', 'boasts', 'stands as'
No false ranges ('from startups to enterprises')
No synonym cycling; repeat the customer's word
Ban era/'Imagine'/'When it comes to' openers, throat-clearing, recap endings, fake-profound kickers, filler transitions
Banned and capped vocabulary (delve, leverage, utilize, seamless, robust...) and empty intensifiers (truly, actually...)
No hedge stacks, puffery, or weasel sources; scope claims honestly
No chummy openers in social ('Great question!', 'Let's be honest')
No exclamation points or hype punctuation in body
No unicode decoration (arrows, bold letters)
No bold label on every bullet, parallel bullet openers, or Title Case
No wisdom-shaped sentences or performed cleverness
No self-narration ('Here's why this matters', 'The takeaway is simple')
No tidy closers; end on a number, named customer, offer, or CTA
Uneven density: let what the writer cares about run longest; no perfect balance
Write as a specific person with real, arguable opinions; first person only when it adds a fact
Never invent experience, stats, or quotes; mark [NEED: ...]
Specificity and swap tests: every claim has a number, name, mechanism, or action
If brand voice / product-marketing context is given, match its tone and register
Make people the subject, not abstract 'the platform enables'

r_rules.text: Output one post as plain text, ready to paste
Block order template: hook, context, body, action, reframe, optional practical block, question, hashtags
Hook is the first paragraph, standalone, 1-2 sentences, ~8-35 words
Hook by post type (mistake+number, stat, 'Unpopular opinion:', 'How to X when Y:', 'We've...')
Short prose paragraphs, blank lines, never one sentence per line
170-280 words in 6-10 blocks
Exactly one takeaway/lesson block after the action (not in announcements)
Bring the hook's number back near the end
Pivot paragraph opens with 'So' or 'Now'
Mistake post order
Data finding post order with 'If your X, do Y before Z' advice paragraph
Opinion post order with 'N reasons' and 'What I'd recommend instead'
How-to post order: hook, role paragraph, numbered moves with why, assumption, question
Announcement post order, CTA to comments, thank-you, no question
Mention role and company size only in how-to and announcement posts
End with one specific question to readers about their experience
Only one question mark; no rhetorical questions in the body
Exactly 3 CamelCase hashtags on the last line
One broad field hashtag plus two topic hashtags
First person: I for decisions, we for company
Plain, measured, honest; own mistakes outright
Hedge claims you cannot prove
No hype, slogans, motivational lines
Use natural contractions
Number formatting: digits for 10+, spell out one to nine in body
Mix sentence lengths, mostly 8-16 words with a few 20-30
No emojis
No exclamation marks
No em dashes
No en dashes or '--'
No bold, headers, or bullet symbols; only '1. ' lists in how-to
No links; send readers to the comments
Reframe phrased as 'looks like X, is really Y'

lessons: Absence-only bans (contrast reveals, negation lists, pile-ons, self-narration, tidy closers) were the biggest miss: when outputs are clean, list the common AI-tell patterns of the genre and ask whether the source bans them, instead of logging them only as 'banned words unknown'.
Per-post caps (one fragment, one list of three, sentences per line) leave no trace in a small sample; ask about frequency limits on rhetorical devices, not just presence.
Check every recovered template phrase against known style bans before shipping it: an inferred device like 'looks like X, is really Y' can itself be a pattern the source forbids.

Express length and formatting in the platform's own units and limits (characters, 'see more' cut, hashtag ranges) and ask whether a value is a target range or an observed coincidence, so narrow observed values (exactly 3 hashtags) are not hardened into rules.
